title: Averaging contracts rotation variation
statement:
Let $n\ge0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $u,v\in\mathbb R$. For independent standard Gaussian vectors $G,G'\in\mathbb R^n$, define $u_u(x)=\int 1_A(\cos u\,x+\sin u\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$ and let $R_A(v)=\Pr(1_A(G)\ne1_A(\cos v\,G+\sin v\,G'))$. Then
\[
\mathbb E\left[|u_u(G)-u_u(\cos v\,G+\sin v\,G')|\right]\le R_A(v).
\]
replaced: Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $\theta\in\mathbb R$, put $u_\theta(x)=\int1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$. For independent $X,Y\sim\gamma_n$, put $R_A(\theta)=\Pr(1_A(X)\ne1_A(\cos\theta\,X+\sin\theta\,Y))$. If $A$ is measurable, then for every $u,v\in\mathbb R$, $\mathbb E_{X,Y}|u_u(X)-u_u(\cos v\,X+\sin v\,Y)|\le R_A(v)$.
